prompt: Players stack armor until they take zero damage and become invincible.
tells: take zero damage and become invincible
why: Use a formula where each armor point helps less, so it never reaches 100%.
trap: Making enemies harder only chases the problem.

prompt: Damage reduction is armor ÷ (armor + 100): 100 armor halves damage, but 200 only cuts it to a third.
why: That formula gives diminishing returns by design.
trap: It isn't random; it's a curve.

prompt: An item stat that increases loot drops makes players wear weaker gear to farm better gear, and the best players feel forced to.
tells: makes players wear weaker gear to farm better gear
why: Capping or curving the stat so it can't dominate is a diminishing-returns fix.
trap: Randomness is the drop; the problem is a stat with no ceiling.

prompt: Movement speed bonuses stack so high that players can skip entire levels.
why: Diminishing returns on speed keep it useful but bounded.
trap: Rebuilding the levels isn't needed; the stat is the problem.

prompt: Cooldown reduction from many items adds up past 100%, making abilities free.
why: Multiply reductions or use a curve so they approach but never reach 100%.
trap: It's a math problem, not a luck problem.

prompt: Each level needs more experience than the last, so leveling slows down as players get stronger.
tells: needs more experience than the last
why: Rising costs per level give diminishing returns on time spent.
trap: It shapes pace, but it isn't the challenge level of enemies.
